statusText: Passed round 7; last edits being re-checked
intro: On Nov 8, 2026, this page was rewritten for readers new to the subject. That version passed a full round of checks (round 7). A few sentences changed afterward, and the newest of those changes have not been re-checked yet, so this page is marked as not finished. An AI agent wrote this page from saved copies of its sources. Separate AI checkers, which never saw the drafting, then checked it in rounds. In this trial, no person checked the facts. Here is what the checkers did, what they found, and what is still open.

sections.title: What we checked
paras: Each round runs the same checks. A page passes a round only when every check passes. After that, we fix only sentences that misstate a source or break our writing rules, and a fresh checker looks again at just those sentences. If a fix changes an evidence label, the whole panel checks the page again.
head: Check
What it does
Pass mark
rows: Code confirms that every sentence cites a source passage or is labeled as our analysis, that quotes match word for word, that numbers appear in the cited passage, that "no party disputes" claims are limited to what we could read, that saved files match their fingerprints, and that the reading level is about grade 8 or lower.
A separate AI checker sees only this page and the source passages. For each sentence it must copy the exact words that support it, and code confirms those words are really there.

Three more AI checkers. One speaks up for Georgia Power's and the manufacturers' positions, one for the PSC's public-interest staff and the advocacy groups, and a neutral editor checks the rules. The editor also asks of each sentence: would we write it the same way about another party?
Both side reviewers give at least 4 of 5, and no serious problem
We hid 12 errors in a copy of the page, such as a wrong number, a quote credited to the wrong party and a wrong deadline time. The fact-checker had to find them without knowing they were there.

sections.title: What each round found
paras: This case has five parties and several separate questions, so it took longer than our other trials. After round 1, no fact-check found a claim its sources didn't support. The reviewers' concerns moved from missing points, to which side's numbers were shown, to one summary line, and then to labels.

sections.title: What's still open
paras: These suggestions would change a card, a label or the balance between parties, so they wait for the next full round. Some contradict each other; we list every view rather than pick one quietly.
items: Reviewers disagree about card 5's label. One says the record shows Georgia Power disputing its first point; one says that rests only on the advocacy group's account of Georgia Power; one says no filing we could read disputes it.

Reviewers disagree about whether the advocacy group's claim that the peak price is set too low belongs on Georgia Power's card, since the group calls rate design outside this case and Georgia Power has asked to strike it.
Each side's reviewer listed points from the record that could strengthen its cards, and asked that its opponents' replies sit in the same fields on every card.
The top of the page and the evidence labels are longer than our budgets, and some technical terms remain.
The parties file briefs on Dec 2, and the PSC is scheduled to decide on Dec 15. This page must be revised as those come in.

sections.title: What this can't do
paras: All the checkers are AI, like the writer, so they may share blind spots. Hiding test errors measures only the kinds of errors we thought to hide.

The checkers compare this page with the sources we saved. They can't tell what is missing from those sources. Some figures and words in the filings are blacked out, one party's testimony is a scan we couldn't use, and one hearing transcript isn't posted.

sections.title: See every report
paras: Every check, report and fix is public in the project's repository, in trials/002-psc-57171-fuel-credit/verification.md.
